title: Disaster scams & false aid offers
label: FRAUD & DOCUMENTS
deck: Pause before paying, sharing identification or following an urgent aid message. Verify the organisation using a contact you find independently, ask for written terms and avoid pressure to pay immediately. Keep emergency funds for verified essentials. A logo, uniform or forwarded link does not establish trust.
tldr: Pause before paying, sharing identification or following an urgent aid message. Verify the organisation using a contact you find independently, ask for written terms and avoid pressure to pay immediately. Keep emergency funds for verified essentials. A logo, uniform or forwarded link does not establish trust.
steps: Use the organisation’s known website or an existing trusted number rather than the contact in an unsolicited message. Confirm the specific programme or provider.
Share only what the verified process needs. Never give account passwords, one-time codes or a full identity document to an unverified caller.
Unexpected upfront fees, gift cards, cryptocurrency or pressure to pay immediately are warning signs. Ask for written terms and time to review.
Verify relevant credentials, references and a written scope before hiring. Do not let a door-to-door offer rush you into unsafe entry or a large advance payment.
Keep receipts and message details without engaging further. Use verified consumer-protection or legal support when safe and available.
next: Warn trusted people privately about confirmed scams without circulating sensitive victim information. If payment or credentials were compromised, contact the relevant bank or provider through a known channel.
watch: An offer of transport or shelter may also carry exploitation risk. Do not surrender documents or separate from family because a stranger promises priority assistance.
without_help: If reporting channels are unavailable, stop contact, protect remaining money and accounts, and retain the records for later. A promised refund is not a reason to make another payment.
household: Assign a trusted adult to each person who needs assistance. Keep medicines, essential contacts and a workable reunion plan with the group. Make decisions around the least mobile person, not the fastest; avoid splitting the family without a clear, safe way to reconnect.
pack_now: Keep essential medicines, safe drinking water, a battery light, footwear, phone power and written contacts accessible. Carry only what you can manage; collecting supplies must not delay escape.
review_status: source-linked editorial review; not independent expert certification
